headline: Sterling's slide is mostly dollar strength. The dollar is near a two-month high because the US-Iran standoff is keeping oil prices up and markets now expect the Fed to raise rates again in October.

drivers.title: Oil and the US-Iran standoff
drivers.text: On Monday the US rejected an Iranian offer that would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz, where the conflict has hampered oil and gas shipping, and Brent crude settled at $105.28 (about £79.60) a barrel. Dearer oil feeds US inflation worries and draws safe-haven money into the dollar.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: The Fed raised rates on 16 September, and markets put about a 65% chance on another quarter-point rise at its 28 October meeting; on Monday traders were almost fully pricing four quarter-point rises over the next 12 months. The dollar index was 101.14 on Tuesday morning, on course for a 1.7% gain in September, its biggest monthly gain since June.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.20% on Friday 25 September, its highest since 2007. Higher yields make holding dollars more rewarding.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: UK 10-year gilt yields are near 5.40%, close to 19-year highs, and the CBI retail survey fell to minus 55 in September against minus 42 expected. The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise.

drivers.title: Where sterling stands
drivers.text: GBP/USD touched a 12-week low near 1.3200 last week and has since steadied between about 1.3220 and 1.3260. Its low for 2026 is 1.3140, set in June.

lower: US core inflation (PCE) on Wednesday at 16:30 Dubai, or Friday's payrolls at 16:30 Dubai, coming in above forecast, which would firm up an October Fed rise.
Further escalation with Iran or in the Gulf that lifts oil again.
Weak UK figures, or a cautious tone from Governor Bailey when he speaks on Thursday at 12:00 Dubai.
higher: US inflation or jobs figures below forecast, which would cut the odds of an October Fed rise.
Progress towards a deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz and brings oil prices down.
Signs that the Bank of England is moving towards a rise in November, after three members voted for one in September.
watch: Friday's US jobs report at 16:30 Dubai is the week's biggest scheduled event for the dollar, and rates can move sharply in the minutes after it.
